source.title: Third-person self-talk facilitates emotion regulation without engaging cognitive control: Converging evidence from ERP and fMRI

confidence_rationale: Direct, converging-methods (ERP + fMRI) neuroscience test of MECH-382's exact claim: referring to oneself in the third person (self-distancing) reduces self-referential emotional reactivity -- a smaller late positive potential within the first second, and reduced medial prefrontal cortex (self-referential) activation -- and does so WITHOUT increasing cognitive-control markers (no extra stimulus-preceding negativity; no increase in cognitive-control fMRI regions). That 'alters processing of the affective/self-referential state, cheaply, without recruiting effortful control' is precisely MECH-382's framing of distancing as a low-effort arbitration-altering operator. Confidence held below 0.8 by modest sample sizes typical of ERP/fMRI studies and by the architectural step from human mPFC self-referential processing to REE's self_reference_frame vocabulary.
failure_signatures: The effect is demonstrated for down-regulating NEGATIVE affect (aversive images, negative autobiographical memories); the paper does not show third-person framing helps with the broader 'sticky high-conflict self-referential state' MECH-382 targets (e.g. unresolved prediction-error pressure), so the generalisation to arbitration-level conflict is an extrapolation.

'Without engaging cognitive control' is an inference from the ABSENCE of increases in a-priori control markers (SPN; control regions); a null on chosen markers is weaker than a positive demonstration that no control was used, so the 'low-effort' premise rests on accepting a null.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Silently referring to oneself by name / in the third person ('Why is Jason feeling this way?') rather than the first person reduces self-referential emotional reactivity: Study 1 (ERP) showed a reduced late positive potential to aversive images within ~1s; Study 2 (fMRI) showed reduced medial prefrontal cortex activation when reflecting on negative memories. Neither study showed increased activity in a-priori cognitive-control markers, suggesting third-person self-talk is a relatively EFFORTLESS form of self-control via psychological distance.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct grounding for MECH-382 (the distancing operator): reframing a sticky first-person state into a more model-like / third-person frame reduces self-referential collapse (the mPFC reduction) and does so cheaply, without an effortful-control surcharge -- exactly MECH-382's claim that distancing alters arbitration via the control plane rather than by spending control resource. Supports the value of the DMN-2 self_reference_frame {first_person, system_state, third_person_model} vocabulary as a functional, not cosmetic, distinction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The evidence is specifically about down-regulating negative AFFECT in humans via natural-language self-reference; MECH-382 targets a broader 'sticky high-conflict self-referential state' (including non-affective prediction-error pressure) reframed through a non-linguistic system-state frame. The 'low-effort' claim rests partly on accepting nulls on chosen control markers.
mapping.source_context: Two human experiments (ERP Study 1; fMRI Study 2) with aversive images and negative autobiographical recall; standard ERP/fMRI sample sizes.

confidence_components.notes: Strong converging-methods design (ERP + fMRI, two studies, a-priori markers) from the group that defined the self-distancing literature; source quality good despite modest n. Mapping fidelity good -- it tests the operator MECH-382 names. Transfer risk elevated: human affect down-regulation via language -> a non-linguistic arbitration-level reframe.
